Acceptance criteria:
If multiple rebate value exist for the same item across different rebate set based on the above mentioned conditions,
The system must evaluate all rebates applicable to the item across different rebate sets.
The system must convert all rebates into comparable values as follows:
If the rebate is an amount, the system must use that amount as the rebate value.

If the rebate amount is defined as a per carton value, the system must convert it to a per unit value while displaying it on the purchase order.
Rebate Per Unit = Rebate Per Carton / Carton Qty  where,
Rebate Per Carton = The rebate amount defined at the carton level for the item

Carton Qty = Carton Qty defined for the item’s supplier in SmartRetailHQ



If the rebate is a percentage, the system must calculate the rebate value as: Rebate Value = (Normal Unit Cost × Rebate%) / 100


The system must compare all rebate values and select the highest rebate.

The system must display the rebate (amount or percentage) corresponding to the highest rebate value for the item.



1.Current: If the rebate is an amount ($/unit), the system is not using that amount, instead converting the value by dividing with carton qty.Expected: If the rebate is an amount ($/unit), the system must use that amount as the rebate value.
2. Current: When multiple rebates are created for an item, one rebate is defined in amount and another rebate defined in per carton value (converted into per unit value), the value displaying in the Rebate column in the Item search grid is different.
Expected: When multiple rebates are created for an item, the system must compare all the rebate values and must display the rebate with highest value.Example: As shown in the uploaded video, when we compare both the rebates (rebate 1 with value: $20/unit and rebate 2 with value: $(10/6=1.66 approx.), the rebate column is being displayed as $3.333 per unit instead of $20 per unit.

Issues.Summary: GCR-T3335 cannot run: reserved t3335Pool of default-less stores is exhausted (Proserpine, Rustic Crumb already configured)
Issues.Description:
## Summary
The automated test GCR-T3335 (a counterpart with no transfer defaults is given them during the add rather than blocking it) aborted in its data setup. The test needs a store without transfer defaults that does not send to Bowen (116). Every store in the reserved t3335Pool, Proserpine (3461) and Rustic Crumb (3590), has already been used. The failure is a test-data exhaustion problem, not a confirmed product defect.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Log in to SmartRetailHQ as a user with the HQ Stock Manager example role.
2. Open ALPHA (9001) in Store Maintenance, go to the Transfers sub-tab and click New in the Receive From section.
3. Select ECHO (9005) as the store, leave Use Defaults checked, click Save and confirm with Yes.
4. In the Add Defaults for Reciprocal Transfer Configuration popup, select Inbound Standard (30), Reciprocal Outbound (24) and cost type Current, then click Save.
5. Open ECHO (9005), go to the Transfers sub-tab and read the Send To section.

Note: the steps are taken from the test case. The run failed on a pool-availability check, so the product behaviour in steps 2 to 5 was not verified (inferred from the test name and error).

## Expected Result
- A store with no transfer defaults is available from t3335Pool.
- The reciprocal defaults popup appears and the save succeeds.
- ALPHA (9001) is listed in the Send To grid of the counterpart store, with Send To Default Reason Code Reciprocal Outbound (24).

## Actual Result
- The test stopped with a data-pool exhaustion error.
- All steps are reported as failed, and the final verification of the counterpart's Send To section was never reached.
- In the network snapshot, Proserpine (3461) and Rustic Crumb (3590) both show an empty send-to list ([]) and so are no longer default-less. The test notes that each run gives one store permanent defaults.

## Error Details
```
Error: GCR-T3335 needs a store WITHOUT transfer defaults that does not send to Bowen (116), and every store in the reserved t3335Pool (Proserpine (3461), Rustic Crumb (3590)) has been used (each run gives one store permanent defaults). Ask the user for new default-less stores and add them to t3335Pool in test-data/HQ/ibt/ibt-stores.json.
```

## Possible Cause
- The test is not repeatable. Each run permanently gives one pool store its transfer defaults, so the two-store pool is used up.
- Inferred from the test name and error: the test needs new default-less stores added to t3335Pool in test-data/HQ/ibt/ibt-stores.json, or a way to reset or clean up store defaults between runs.
- The step 4 text mentions ECHO (9005), but the error comes from the pool check, which suggests the test selects its counterpart from t3335Pool at runtime.
